F. Kesser, Esq.,
Hon. Secretary,
International Committee for the Organisation
of European Immigrants in China,
Sassoon House,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have to refer to your letter dated November 24,
enclosing a copy of a letter to the Acting Deputy Treasurer -
Revenue on the subject of tax remission for the premises of
your Organisation. Whilst the Council fully appreciates the
valuable services rendered by the Organisation, I must state
that the Council's policy governing rate remission is strictly
applied, and any concession granted on the grounds of services
to the Council, as set forth in your letter to the Acting
Deputy Treasurer - Revenue, would be a deviation from this
policy and set an undesirable precedent.

In conclusion I would state that the Council has
carefully reconsidered your request for tax remission on
charitable grounds, but I regret to inform you that there
is nothing further to add to the Deputy Secretary's letter
to you dated October 30 on this subject.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,

G. Godfrey Phillips

Secretary & Commissioner General.

先生：

谨提及阁下11月24日来信，信中附有一份致代理副财政司（税务）关于贵机构用房免税事宜的信件副本。虽然工部局充分赞赏该机构所提供的宝贵服务，但我必须声明，工部局关于减免捐税的政策得到严格执行，而如阁下致代理副财政司（税务）的信中所述，以服务于工部局为由给予任何让步，将偏离这一政策并开不良先例。

最后，我要说明的是，工部局已仔细重新考虑了阁下基于慈善理由提出的免税请求，但我很遗憾地通知阁下，在此事项上，除10月30日副秘书致阁下的信函内容外，并无更多补充。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，

G. Godfrey Phillips

秘书兼总 commissioner。

CENTRAL REGISTRY OF ALL IMMIGRANTS.
This Registry has some 16,000 cards which are marked with full particulars and contain a photograph of the respective immigrant. It has been a rule that a person who is not thus registered cannot claim assistance from either the "I.C." or the "Committee for the Assistance of European Refugees in Shanghai". DISPOSAL OF PROPERTIES.
The "I.C." has been authorised by the German Consulate to attend inquests of German "J" citizens, and to assume the same authority re the disposal of the property of the deceased which a Consular representative would have. It also assists needy refugees by redeeming their pawned property and returning it to the respective owners; the redemption fee is collected by instalments.

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE

Shanghai 24th November, 1941.

The Deputy Treasurer - Revenue,
Finance Department, Revenue Office
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

Sir,

This is to acknowledge the receipt of your letter
dated November 20, 1941, wherein you repeat your previous
statement that the tax-regulations do not permit the remission
of taxation, where Headquarters of charitable organisations
are concerned.

I regret that I cannot leave this matter rest,
because I feel that if such regulations have existed in
the past, that is not a reason why they could not be amended
with a view to alleviate the financially difficult
position which Charity Organisations find themselves in
at present. Apart from this, I would observe that this
Organisation has been, and still is, rendering services
to the Shanghai Municipal Council and its various Departments,
free of charge, which are of considerable value, to say the
least. It might interest you to learn that the premises
taxed by you contain an extensive card-index of nearly
20,000 records and photos of Central European Immigrants,
of which the Police has been making use on numerous
occasions. I do not wish to enlarge upon this subject,
but leave it to you to obtain verification of these facts
from the Department-Chiefs concerned.

Under these circumstances, the exemption of our
premises from taxation should be granted as a token of the
Council's appreciation for the work done by the "I.C."

I would appreciate it very much, if you would
submit my letter to the Council for renewed consideration
of my request to exempt the "I.C." premises from the pay-
ment of General Municipal Rate . I take it that it is not
necessary for me to submit a request for exemption from
the payment of the Special Business Tax.

Yours faithfully,

(Sgd.) Paul Komor

Hon. Secretary.

The Secretary & Commissioner General.

Letter dated November 24, from the
International Committee for the Organization
of European Immigrants in China, requesting
reconsideration of the Council's decision to
refuse to grant remission of taxation on the
premises occupied by their Committee at 70.20
Nanking Road.

I would refer to my report dated October 30, 1941 on
this subject which shows clearly that these premises are non-
exemptable under the Council's ruling applicable to rate
remission in respect of charity organizations.

The claim that this organization renders valuable
services to the Council is irrelevant and any concession on
these grounds would create an undesirable precedent.

I recommend, therefore, that the International Committee
for the Organization of European Immigrants in China be informed
that no departure can be made from the Council's fixed rule
governing rate remission which is strictly applied.

Copies of letter dated November 17 from the "I.C." and
my reply dated November 20, 1941 are annexed.

P. Bonney.
Acting Deputy Treasurer - Revenue.

Chinese Maritime Customs,

Shanghai, 15th July 1940.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge your communication
of the 12th instant, in regard to International Settlement
Municipal Police seeking co-operation of Customs River Police
when boarding vessels in harbour to implement the regulations
restricting the entry of Jewish refugees into Shanghai, and,
also, inviting the nomination of a Customs River Police
officer to maintain a constant liaison with Municipal Police.
And in reply thereto, I agree to such co-operation as re-
quested, and would suggest that the liaison be maintained
between the Municipal Police and River Police Headquarters,
situate in the Harbour Master's Office Building, opposite
the Custom House, The Bund.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient Servant,

Y. Sugiyama

Harbour Master

July 12, 40.

Y. Sugiyama, Esq.,
Harbour Master (Additional),
Harbour Master's Office,
Chinese Maritime Customs,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter of
June 28 and my acknowledgement of June 29, on the subject
of the functioning of the Municipal Police on vessels in
the harbour in connection with the entry of Jewish refugees.

I have to assure you that the Municipal Police
will gladly seek the co-operation of the Customs River
Police in carrying out measures on ships in the harbour
designed merely to implement the regulations restricting
the entry of Jewish refugees into Shanghai. As you are
doubtless aware, these regulations were drawn up by the
Settlement Authorities in consultation with the Japanese
Authorities.

I wish to avail myself of this opportunity to
invite your nomination of an officer of the Customs River
Police with whom the Municipal Police would be very
pleased to maintain a constant liaison.

I have the honour to be,

Sir,

Your obedient Servant,

G. Godfrey Phillips

Secretary & Commissioner General.

本人须向阁下保证，工部局警务处将乐意寻求海关水警的合作，以在港内船只上实施旨在仅仅落实限制犹太难民进入上海规定的措施。想必阁下知悉，这些规定是租界当局与日本当局协商后制定的。

本人愿借此机会，请阁下提名一名海关水警官员，工部局警务处将非常乐意与其保持常设联络。
